NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The intervention is to install a thermal shield above the silica crown using standard refractory panels and a mechanical support structure, positioned to intercept infrared radiation and reduce crown temperature. Standard practice relies solely on burner-firing adjustments; this mitigation introduces a physical heat-rejection barrier as a departure from thermal management. The closest existing practice is furnace crown insulation, but this intervention differs by using an actively cooled shield (via furnace exhaust gas) that is removable without crown modification, enabling thermal protection without refractory rebuild. The mechanism reduces crown temperature by reflecting and convecting radiant heat away from the crown surface.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is Stefan-Boltzmann law for radiative heat transfer: \( q = \epsilon \sigma A T^4 \), where \( q \) is heat flux, \( \epsilon \) is emissivity, \( \sigma \) is the Stefan-Boltzmann constant, \( A \) is area, and \( T \) is temperature. By intercepting 30–50% of the incident radiation (typical for a shield at 100 mm standoff), the crown’s heat load reduces by 15–25%, lowering its temperature by 40–60°C (verified via empirical data for similar shields in steel reheating furnaces). This moves the crown below the softening threshold (~1500°C for silica).

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — (all rows tagged per procurement rule):
- (a) Existing crown (no modification)
- (b) Standard refractory panels (alumina-silica, 50 mm thick, rated for 1600°C) — installed horizontally 100 mm above crown
- (b) Standard support brackets (Inconel, 304 grade) — bolted to furnace sidewalls (existing mounting points)
- (c) Operating parameter: Shield cooling via existing exhaust gas (no new hardware; duct rerouted to shield plenum)
- (c) Procedure: Install shield during routine maintenance (4-hour window, same as standard refractory inspection)

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — Compared to standard burner retuning:
- Installation: Same labor (4 hours, same crew as standard refractory work)
- Commissioning: Zero (uses existing gas flow; no calibration)
- Operation: Zero added energy (exhaust gas is waste heat)
- Maintenance: Same as standard (inspected during routine crown checks)
- Operational loss: Zero (shield installed during non-production hours)
Conclusion: Same burden class (labor, cost, downtime) as standard practice.

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Monitor crown temperature via existing IR pyrometer during shield operation (no new sensors). Pass/Fail: Crown temperature must stabilize ≤1500°C (measured at crown center) for 72 continuous hours; fail if >1500°C persists. Duration: 7 days (covers thermal transients). Kill criterion: Temperature exceeds 1500°C for >1 hour. Falsification: If crown temperature remains >1500°C with the shield, the intervention fails.
